answer: Special Ops provenance rule: borrow trust that took years to grow elsewhere. Each identity must anchor itself to one outside history, such as a code account whose patches were merged by unrelated maintainers, proven by a signed challenge, and each history can back only one key. Pay scales with the anchor's age and stranger-merged work. Faking that means farming years of accepted patches per key across a cold tundra of reviewers, while an honest agent with one violet thread of real contributions walks right in.
